messages:
anita: RFC follow-up: who owns private endpoint NAT & route for multi-customer workspace? Need decision for rollout.

matt: Short answer: ownership should live with infra control plane unless customer opts into dedicated gateway.

li: Agree. Key risk is SNAT pool exhaustion and noisy-tenant impact.

carla: If infra owns, billing attribution becomes messy. How do we split egress costs?

anita: Two options sketched in RFC: shared-peering (one egress NAT per region) vs per-tenant-gateway (dedicated ENI/NAT). Need tradeoffs.

matt: Shared: simpler ops, cheaper, faster onboarding. Per-tenant: isolation, clear billing, higher infra footprint.

raj: Also consider TLS termination. If termination happens at our gateway we can L7 route, else need SNI passthrough and certs at tenant side.

li: Operationally, SNAT IP mapping must be stable for customer allowlists. Shared NAT breaks that.

carla: Could we do sticky IPs per-tenant on top of shared NAT by allocating small IP block per tenant? Cost vs complexity?

anita: Prototype idea: ephemeral-lease mapping service that pins an ephemeral secondary IP to a tenant for the session lifetime. Thoughts?

matt: Sounds complex; failure modes? what if lease server down?

li: Fallback plan: fall back to shared pool and emit a change event for tenant. Need clear SLA.

sre-bot: Incident: previous test showed 2min window where SNAT remap caused request failures. Link: https://go/incident/1234

carla: :eyes: ok that incident favors dedicated.

raj: Billing: we can tag flows with tenant-id in VPC Flow logs and attribute costs later. But customers needing static IPs won't accept that.

anita: Proposed compromise for rollout: 1) default = shared NAT + per-tenant IP reservations for customers who need static IPs (paid). 2) allow dedicated gateways as enterprise opt-in. 3) rollout telemetry and cheap eval window.

matt: We also need model for burst capacity: 'burst pools' that can be assigned temporarily to tenants.

li: Add config shape suggestion:

```
egressPolicy:
  mode: shared|reserved|dedicated
  reservedIPs: 2
  burstPool: true
```

carla: Who owns the config? Product or infra? Ops needs final say.

anita: Infra owns implementation; Product owns UX + pricing. We'll draft a rollout PR.

matt: I'll stub the operator API today. Will post link.

matt: PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/555

ops-bot: Reminder: update runbook for SNAT remap, include steps to reassign leases and notify customers.

anita: Action items: @matt open PR (inflight), @li run load tests for ephemeral leasing, @carla draft pricing language, infra to propose monitoring signals. Meeting Friday 9am. :calendar:
